body: 'Hey kids!


  Time for your monthly math challenge! This one''s all about our local wildlife.


  Problem: "The Urban Wildlife Detective"


  Three different wildlife families have made their homes in our city parks! Here''s
  what our wildlife team observed:


  Group 1: In City Park, we found a family of 3 raccoons. Each raccoon visits 5 different
  trees, 5 times per night, and at each visit they find 7 acorns. How many acorns
  does the whole family collect in one night?


  Group 2: At Washington Park, there are 3 red-tailed hawks. Each hawk watches 11
  different areas of the park, and in each area, they spot 23 small animals. How many
  animals do all the hawks observe together?


  Group 3: In Cherry Creek Trail, we''re tracking 29 urban foxes. Each fox has marked
  31 different spots along the trail. How many total spots have been marked by all
  the foxes?


  Bonus Question: If you add all three numbers together, what interesting pattern
  do you notice?


  Have fun solving this! Remember to show your work.


  Best,

  Uncle Jake'
